samples.summary: No test covers the `saved-locally` state ever reaching the chip — `useSyncStatus` never passes `durable`
samples.evidence: `deriveSyncState` gained a `durable` input and a new `saved-locally` state (sync-state.ts:70-85), and `tests/components/sync-status/sync-state.test.ts` exercises the pure function. But the only production caller, `use-sync-status.ts:214`, calls `deriveSyncState({ connected, pending, syncFailed })` with no `durable` argument, and nothing else in src computes it. So the entire user-facing value of the feature is unreachable in the app and no test would fail. The chip suite (`tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx`) has no case for `saved-locally`, and its existing case 'does not claim the work is stored locally' (line 379) still passes precisely because durability never arrives.

samples.summary: New chip state `saved-locally` (label, icon, tooltip, and the deliberate absence of the warning toast / unload guard) has no chip-level test
samples.evidence: sync-status-chip.tsx adds LABELS['saved-locally'], ICONS['saved-locally'] and a bespoke tooltip paragraph, and `stranded`/`mayHaveUnsent` (lines 106-109) deliberately exclude the new state so no beforeunload prompt, navigation guard or red toast fires. None of that is asserted anywhere: `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` contains no `saved-locally` case. If the state were wired up wrongly (e.g. it kept the destructive styling, or lost the guard for work that is not actually durable) nothing in the suite would fail.

samples.summary: Recovery only tested for `sheet`; the `doc`, `slides`, `board` and `note` rebuild paths are untested
samples.evidence: `readContent` (offline-copy-recovery.ts:39-86) has branches for doc/slides/board built on YorkieDocStore/YorkieSlidesStore/YorkieBoardStore, and `writeNote` (line ~147) handles notes via a live `Client`. `offline-copy-recovery.test.ts` only ever archives a sheet-shaped root and calls with `type: 'sheet'` (plus an 'image' refusal and an unreadable archive). A wrong reader for doc/slides/board would hand the user an empty or plausible-but-wrong 'offline copy' of work that the SDK already dropped — the last copy of it — and no test would catch it. The note path is not executed at all.

samples.summary: No test asserts the durable store is constructed with the cross-tab `isOpenElsewhere` guard
samples.evidence: `DurableYorkieProvider` builds `new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId, isOpenElsewhere: isOpenInAnyTab })` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:77-88), and the store's own suite (wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts, 'documents open in another tab') shows that without that callback one tab's eviction/sweep deletes another tab's open document and its later appends silently vanish. The only component-level assertion is `expect(mounted[0].store).toBeDefined()` in collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx, which holds for any object — including a store constructed without `isOpenElsewhere` or with the wrong `userId`. The wiring that prevents cross-tab data loss is therefore untested.

samples.summary: `LockRefusalWatch` (the ErrDocumentOpenElsewhere backstop) is never exercised — the test mocks `useYorkie` to report no error
samples.evidence: collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx mocks `useYorkie: () => ({ client: undefined, loading: false, error: undefined })` and its own comment concedes 'No error here means it never fires'. No test drives an error with `code === 'ErrDocumentOpenElsewhere'` into the watcher, nor the negative case that another error code leaves the election alone. A typo in the string constant, or firing on every error, would ship undetected; `use-durable-document.test.tsx` only tests `standDown()` called directly.

samples.summary: Negative durable cases assert only `mounted === []` and never that the editor still renders, so a blank-screen regression passes
samples.evidence: 'never persists a PDF comment document', 'does not mount a second durable client...' and 'stays on the ambient client when the build cannot carry a key' assert only on the recorded `mounted` array. `CollabDocumentProvider` returns `null` while `!settled`, so a bug that left those documents permanently unsettled — a blank editor for every PDF/second tab — satisfies these assertions exactly as well as correct behaviour does. Only the two cases that mount durably assert `getByTestId('child')`.

samples.summary: Erase-on-disable, stale collection and the recovery hand-back exist only as unwired units; no test covers (and no code performs) their app-level installation
samples.evidence: grep over packages/frontend/src (excluding tests) shows `watchForOfflineDisable`, `collectStale`, `listRecoverableWork` and `recoverOfflineCopy` have no production call sites, and `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled` is consumed only by `use-durable-document.ts` — there is no Settings toggle. The units are well tested in isolation, but nothing tests (because nothing implements) that the promise quoted in offline-erase.ts — 'turning this off deletes them' — or the 30-day sweep actually happens in the running app.

samples.summary: The cross-instance `touch()` on load (the shared-DB half of the 'don't evict an open document' guard) has no test
samples.evidence: `load()` both adds to the in-memory `touched` set and fires `void this.touch(docKey)` to move `updatedAt` in the database, explicitly so *other* instances see the document as recently used. Every cleanup test that covers this ('never evicts a document this session has open', 'does not collect a document another instance has open') is satisfied either by `touched` or by the injected `isOpenElsewhere`; none reopens a second instance after a bare `load()` and checks that the entry is no longer the oldest candidate. If `touch()` silently stopped working, nothing fails.

samples.summary: Comment points coverage at a test file that does not exist
samples.evidence: The new comment says '`durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` covers the nesting', but no such file exists (glob over packages/frontend/src/components/**/durable* returns only durable-yorkie-provider.tsx). The nesting is covered by `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx`; the stale pointer overstates where to look for coverage.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: `deriveSyncState` gained `durable`/`saved-locally` (sync-state.ts:48,66-88), but the sole production caller `use-sync-status.ts:214` passes only `{connected, pending, syncFailed}`, and a repo-wide grep for `deriveSyncState|saved-locally|Saved to this device|IconDeviceDesktop` finds no other computation of durability in src. Consequently no rendered test can reach the state: the chip suites drive the real `useSyncStatus` over a mocked `@yorkie-js/react` doc (sync-status-chip.test.tsx:6-7) and none of their 16 cases covers `saved-locally`; the case at line 379-389 asserts the absence of that wording and passes vacuously. The only durable coverage is the pure-function table in sync-state.test.ts:60-133. The chip's new label/icon/tooltip branch (sync-status-chip.tsx:41,52,64-80) is untested new user-facing behavior. The repo's own task file (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:95-99,175) independently records the wiring as not done and the state as unreachable. I searched sync-status tests, navigation/site-header/shared-header suites, and the whole repo for the distinctive strings; found no counterexample.

verdict.reason: The chip really does add a fifth state with new user-facing surface and a deliberate safety-guard exclusion, and nothing renders it in a test. sync-status-chip.tsx:41,52,64-80 add the label 'Saved to this device', the IconDeviceDesktop icon and a bespoke tooltip; lines 106-109 exclude 'saved-locally' from `mayHaveUnsent`, so the beforeunload handler (119-130), useNavigationGuard (142-158), the warning toast (164-198) and the `text-destructive` styling (226) never fire for it. Searching repo-wide for 'Saved to this device'/'saved-locally'/'IconDeviceDesktop' turns up only sync-state.test.ts (pure deriveSyncState reducer, never renders the chip) and a negative assertion in sync-status-chip.test.tsx:388. Both chip test files (sync-status-chip.test.tsx, sync-status-chip-navigation.test.tsx) and the header tests contain no durable/saved-locally case, and every consumer of useSyncStatus/SyncStatusChip was grepped for an indirect test; no e2e specs exist. So a regression that restored destructive styling, broke the tooltip wording, or dropped the guard for work that is not actually durable would fail nothing. No counterexample found.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: readContent (offline-copy-recovery.ts:39-88) branches on sheet/doc/slides/board with three different store-backed readers, and a separate note path (lines 126-135 → readNote:91-94 → writeNote:159-179). The only test file that imports recoverOfflineCopy is offline-copy-recovery.test.ts, and all six of its cases pass type 'sheet' (lines 94, 111, 134, 162, 194) except one passing 'image' to assert the unsupported-type refusal (line 177). verdict.reason: The provider builds `new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId, isOpenElsewhere: isOpenInAnyTab })` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:76-87) and `isOpenElsewhere` is optional in the store options (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:137, 291-310), so omitting it compiles fine. I searched repo-wide for `isOpenElsewhere|isOpenInAnyTab`, `DurableYorkieProvider|durable-yorkie-provider`, `WafflebaseDocStore`, "another tab"/"cross-tab", all frontend test globs, `*.spec.ts`, and `**/*{durable,offline}*`; no test imports the provider at all (the comment at collab-document-provider.test.tsx:23 refers to a `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` that does not exist).
